raw_response:
Alright, another year. Me and the old lady, it's just the two of us now — the kids have moved off to work in the city. We got our 9 mu, half of it's the wheat that's already in the ground, and after that comes in come the maize. Same rotation as my father's time. No reason to change what works.

The wheat went in last October, right after the maize came off. Planted the regular variety the co-op sells — Jimai something, I just ask for what everyone else is buying. About 30 jin of seed per mu, same as always. Put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, that's the 15-15-15, 50 kilos to the bag, cost me about 100 yuan. Gave it the winter water back in December before the ground froze hard.

Come spring, when the wheat greens up and starts jointing, I'll topdress urea — around 30 jin a mu. I know Old Wang down the way uses 40, but for me 30's been enough all these years, and 40 costs more money I don't have sitting around. I'll run the well that same time to wash it in, and then if it looks dry at grain filling I'll water one more time. So three waterings total counting the winter one. For pests, I'll spray herbicide for the broadleaf weeds in spring, and if aphids come around flowering I'll spray once more. That's it. Harvest in early June — I hire the combine that comes through the village, pay by the mu.

Right behind the combine, the maize goes in. Can't waste a day because the season's short. I buy hybrid seed from the township shop — Zhengdan or whatever they got that year, costs more than saved seed but yields better, everyone plants hybrid now. Don't plow — just direct seed into the wheat stubble with the seeder we rent from the co-op. Put down another bag of compound at planting. Then at big bell stage in July I topdress urea, maybe 40 jin a mu — maize eats more than wheat, everybody knows that.

Summer's wet usually, so if the rains come on time I won't water the maize at all. But if July goes dry I'll run the well once at tasseling. Spray herbicide once early after planting. If corn borer gets bad I'll spray, otherwise I leave it alone. Harvest end of September and the cycle starts over.

Last year the wheat gave me about 500 kilos a mu and maize about 530. A decent year, not the best. I'm figuring about the same this year if the weather behaves. For money, all in, maybe 7-8 thousand yuan for the year across both crops. It's tight but the grain subsidy helps, and we keep our flour and sell the rest. At 55, I'm not looking to chase bigger yields by spending more. What I do works, my neighbors do about the same, and the land knows me.
